newsitem.title: USA: Computer Sciences wins U.S. Army contract.
newsitem.headline: Computer Sciences wins U.S. Army contract.

text.p: Computer Sciences Corp said on Wednesday it was awarded a contract from the U.S. Army, with an estimated potential value of $740 million, to provide systems engineering and technical assistance at the U.S. Army Space and Strategic Defense Command in Alabama.
Three other companies were awarded contracts in the procurement, Computer Sciences said -- Mevatec, Nichols Research Corp and Teledyne Brown Engineering.
The multiple-award, indefinite delivery and quantity contract would be worth about $740 million if all options were exercised over a five-year performance period, Computer Sciences said.
Computer Sciences said it would support the Army's Space and Strategic Defense Command and the program executive office for air and missile defense offices in Huntsville, Alabama.
These offices manage the Army's research and development efforts in air and missile defense, the company said.

The company said it would also provide assistance to Space and Strategic Defense Command headquarters in Washington, D.C., the Army Space Command in Colorado and the High Energy Laser Systems test facility in New Mexico.
Computer Sciences said there were 10 subcontractors, including the Space and Science Technology Alliance, an Alabama university consortium.

Other teammates were ANRO Engineering, Camber Corp, EARTH TECH, EER Systems, JB Systems Engineering Support Co, Kaman Sciences Corp, Quality Research Inc, Systems Development Corp and Tybrin Corp, the company said.
